reviewedBy: Oza (repository owner), accepting the automated code audit's findings on 2026-07-28. Prepared by the audit; reviewed and accepted by the owner.
reason: Correction to Egypt's bracket-exclusion (tiering) rule. No tax band, rate, personal exemption, NOSI rate or NOSI cap was changed: ETA_BANDS is byte-for-byte the same seven bands (0% to 40,000; 10% to 55,000; 15% to 70,000; 20% to 200,000; 22.5% to 400,000; 25% to 1,200,000; 27.5% above), matching PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries for Egypt and the Andersen Egypt 2026 table. What changed is how the exclusion rule is applied. Egypt's tiering rule WITHDRAWS the lower brackets once net taxable income passes a threshold and taxes the income they covered at the first surviving rate; it re-rates income already counted rather than adding a surcharge. Every implementation instead carried a typed table of bandWidth x that band's OWN rate (0 / 1,500 / 2,250 / 26,000 / 45,000 / 200,000 or 274,750), which is the tax the withdrawn band had already collected, and the four implementations disagreed about how to combine it: egypt/eg-paye.html and the Swahili copy summed every entry passed, while assets/js/engines/eg-paye.js and netlify/functions/_engines/eg-paye.js took only the last. Neither produced the statutory figure. The backend's reading was provably impossible, returning an effective rate of 43.6% at 1,300,000 gross and 40.5% at 1,600,000 against a 27.5% top marginal rate. The table has five exclusion tiers, not six: thresholds 600,000 / 700,000 / 800,000 / 900,000 / 1,200,000. The 1,000,000 tier the code carried does not exist in the published table, and the 25% bracket is never withdrawn. Correct extras, now DERIVED from ETA_BANDS rather than typed, are 4,000 / 6,750 / 10,250 / 15,250 / 25,250, each being (income the withdrawn brackets covered x the first surviving rate) - (standard band tax already charged on that income). Verified two ways: the derived model was checked against the published tier table transcribed independently as six columns of surviving brackets, and reproduced it exactly at 25 points including every threshold boundary; and tests/paye-implementation-parity.test.js now asserts all four implementations against that transcribed table at 14 salaries and sweeps 199 salaries from 50,000 to 5,000,000 confirming no effective rate exceeds 27.5%. Also in this change: the Swahili copy read rule.extraTax from a table whose field the translation pass had renamed to extraKodi, so its exclusionExtra was 0 + undefined = NaN and every Egyptian salary above roughly 639,000 gross rendered a NaN tax; the same pass left standardKodi destructured as standardTax. Both are fixed, and /sw/egypt/kikokotoo-kodi-mshahara/ is added to this tool's routes so that copy is inside the digest gate for the first time. Separately, getMarginalRate returned rate * 100, which is 27.500000000000004 for 0.275 in binary floating point and was rendered straight into the displayed marginal rate; it is now rounded to one decimal place. Sources read: Deloitte Middle East 'Amendment introduced to tax brackets' (the tiering table with dashes marking withdrawn brackets, at the Law 175/2023 thresholds) and Andersen Egypt 'Egypt's Personal Income Tax in 2026' (the same six-column table at the current 40,000 / 55,000 / 70,000 thresholds). Both publish five exclusion tiers and neither publishes a 1,000,000 tier. Bracket values themselves cross-checked against PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries. The Egyptian Tax Authority's own portal was not reachable to read the operative article directly, so per .claude/rules/salary-tax.md no 'Last verified' stamp was advanced by this change and the page's existing planning-grade framing is unchanged.

fixtureDeltas.why: NATI 960,860 falls in the 900,000-1,200,000 tier. Correct extra is 15,250 (first 200,000 re-rated from a standard 29,750 to 200,000 x 22.5% = 45,000). The engine previously applied 26,000, the tax the withdrawn 20% band had already collected. Standard band tax on 960,860 is 214,965 either way, so the taxpayer was overcharged 10,750.
Follows tax.netTax; NOSI of 19,140 is unchanged.

Top tier. Correct extra is 25,250 (first 400,000 re-rated from a standard 74,750 to 400,000 x 25% = 100,000). The engine previously applied 274,750, which is the whole cumulative standard tax at 1,200,000 rather than the incremental re-rating. Difference 274,750 - 25,250 = 249,500.
Follows tax.netTax; NOSI is capped at 19,140 and unchanged.
Unchanged. No exclusion tier is reached at zero income.
